title: Shock law
description: The probability distribution of one shock in a parameter file: a positive random variable with mean one. Draft; see shock-laws.md.
$comment: This validator checks names, types and ranges only. The checker checks what JSON Schema cannot express: orderings, sums, means, bot < top, and the rules for tables. Each law is a mapping with one key, the law's name.

ShockLaw.$comment: The accepted laws. Formula and Code, defined below, are reserved for a later version and deliberately left out of this list, so a file that uses either fails validation.

TruncationBound.description: A truncation bound in standard deviations of the normal before truncation. Left out, it is three standard deviations (-3 below, 3 above); null means no bound on that side.

Degenerate.description: psi = 1: the shock is switched off.

TruncatedLogNormal.description: ln psi = mu + s * Z, with Z standard normal conditioned on bot <= Z <= top. sd_log is the standard deviation of ln psi after truncation, so s = sd_log / sqrt(Var(Z | bot <= Z <= top)); mu is set so that E[psi] = 1 after truncation.
TruncatedLogNormal.$comment: An omitted bound is three standard deviations; null is no bound. The checker refuses null on both sides, which is LogNormal, and requires bot < top. The ontology's chart: PD_0000032.

Uniform.description: psi ~ U[1 - half_width, 1 + half_width], in levels.

Discrete.description: psi takes the stated values with the stated probabilities. The points are the model, not a quadrature.
Discrete.$comment: The checker requires equal lengths, strictly increasing values, probabilities summing to one, and a mean of one.

LogNormalMixture.description: ln psi = c + X, with X drawn from normal components, component j with probability weight_j, mean mean_log_j and standard deviation sd_log_j, and one common shift c making E[psi] = 1.
LogNormalMixture.$comment: The checker requires weights summing to one, the weighted mean of mean_log equal to zero, and components in increasing order of mean_log, then of sd_log. The ontology's chart: PD_0000054.

TruncatedLogNormalMixture.description: ln psi = c + X, with X drawn from truncated normal components, each with its mean_log and sd_log stated after truncation and its bounds in standard deviations of its normal before truncation, as for TruncatedLogNormal, and one common shift c making E[psi] = 1.
TruncatedLogNormalMixture.$comment: An omitted bound is three standard deviations; null is no bound. The checker requires weights summing to one, the weighted mean of mean_log equal to zero, components in increasing order of mean_log, then sd_log, bot and top, bot < top in each, and some component truncated: with none, the law is LogNormalMixture. The ontology's chart: PD_0000058.

Tabulated.description: A user's own law, given as its quantile function: points (u, Q(u)) for u from 0 to 1, with Q linear in u between consecutive points. The table is the law, not an approximation of one.
Tabulated.$comment: The checker requires: first u 0 and last u 1, neither repeated; u never falling, an interior value at most twice and consecutively; Q never falling; at least one stretch where u and Q both rise, and not a single rising stretch (Uniform); no interior point exactly collinear with its neighbors; mean one to within 1e-12.

Formula.description: RESERVED, not accepted yet: a law given as a mathematical expression for its quantile function, density or CDF.
Formula.$comment: Candidate languages: Content MathML (how SBML states its math, and the basis of its Distributions package), or a small text grammar with a reference parser in each supported language. The checker would verify mean one and the regularity conditions by numerical integration. See shock-laws.md.

Code.description: RESERVED, not accepted yet: a law given as compiled functions behind a fixed interface, such as quantile(u), cdf(x), pdf(x) and support().
Code.$comment: Candidate forms: C source, or WebAssembly for identical behavior on every platform; the file identified by its SHA-256. Precedent: the Functional Mock-up Interface. Open questions: running other people's code, reproducibility across platforms, toolkits that cannot call C, and a hash that identifies the file rather than the law. See shock-laws.md.
